title.en: Gesture arbitration between camera orbit and a committed move

summary: Check that one gesture yields at most one legal move and that cancellation leaves state and history untouched.
objective: Committed gestures add at most one move under the declared history policy, cancelled gestures change nothing, and arbitration holds for the whole drag.
applies_when: A viewer turns a puzzle by dragging directly on its surface.
The same input device also orbits the camera.
Drags can start on edges, leave the object or lose pointer capture.
intent_signals: dragging near an edge turns the wrong layer
the layer stayed half turned after I let go
example_prompts: Check the drag-to-turn arbitration of this puzzle scene.

principles: A gesture proposes and the move engine decides: the interaction layer owns a temporary angle, and only a committed legal move changes state.
One gesture produces at most one move, so arbitration between orbiting the camera and turning a layer is resolved once and then held for the duration of the drag.

Cancellation is a first-class outcome, and which events cause it is an authored policy: releasing below the commit threshold usually cancels, while a release outside the object under valid pointer capture may legitimately commit. Declare the policy for off-surface release and for capture loss, then check that policy.
implementation: Record for every gesture the initial contact point and surface, the inferred axis and layer, the accumulated angle and the final decision.

Script the ambiguous cases against the declared policy: a drag starting on an edge between two faces, a drag that reverses direction, a drag released off the object while capture is held, a capture loss mid-drag, and a modifier-driven camera orbit starting on a face.
For each case record state and history length before and after, and whether the temporary angle returned to zero.
Test the commit threshold from both sides with the same starting contact, just below and just above.
observable_checks: Every gesture yields at most one committed move, and history grows according to the declared transaction policy: by exactly one per commit when moves are not coalesced, and by the declared coalesced amount otherwise, while cancelled gestures add nothing.
A cancelled gesture leaves the exact state unchanged and returns the temporary presentation angle to zero, with no partially rotated layer left behind.
Once arbitration selects camera orbit or layer turn, that choice holds for the whole drag; a mid-drag switch is reported as an arbitration defect.

known_limits: Covers input arbitration and commitment; it does not evaluate how the gesture feels or whether the threshold suits a particular audience.
Authored verification guidance; no interface was run for this record.
creative_affordances: Adapt the scenario, scale and presentation to your subject; this record fixes what must be checked, not how the scene must look.
